AccessLogEntry.description: One access in words a patient can read. A staff identifier is never in it.

roles.description: Empty for `you` and for rows older than role recording.

AccessLogPage.description: Newest first, 50 a page. `next` is the `before` for the older page, or null.

AcknowledgeReferral.description: The referrer has seen this version. Anything but the current version is a 409; so is a repeat. A referral the caller did not send is a 404.

overdue.description: The date to check it with the person has passed.

AllergyList.description: Every allergy in every status, the no-known-allergies statement, the banner summary and amendment notices by allergy id. The statement, summary and notices are described only as objects.

AllergyRecord.description: One allergy as recorded. An absent optional field means not stated; criticality is never defaulted to low.

system.description: A URI; a SNOMED CT code is checked.

no_known_allergies.description: false when the statement was withdrawn.

notice.description: What a reader of the record must be told; null when there is nothing to tell (seen after a withdrawal).

extension.description: The written reason for the one extension, once taken.

state.description: Tagged by state; accepted, applied and denied carry their own fields.

AssessmentForm.description: One version of a form, from `src/assessment_forms.toml`. Empty approver and day mean a draft.

items.description: Every question once: a value (a boolean for yes-no, a listed string for a choice), or null with absent_reason.

AuditBroken.description: 409: a row was found altered. A monitor that reads only the status still notices.

AuditHead.description: The chain's head: publish it where the database's owner cannot write, and pass it back as a checkpoint.

AuditRow.description: One audit row as an auditor sees it. A search leaves the digests out; an export adds `digest` and `prev_digest` so the chain can be re-verified elsewhere.

detail.description: Structured detail; never demographics or consent content.

patient.description: Patient/<id> when the access named one.

AuditSearch.description: Up to one page, newest first. `next` is the `before` for the following page, or null at the end.

AuditUnchecked.description: 424: nothing was found wrong, but some rows could not be checked because this service does not hold the key that made their digest. A key problem, not evidence of tampering.

AuditVerified.description: 200: the chain checked out. `assurance` says in words what that does and does not prove.

overdue.description: Unreviewed for longer than the review window; never true once reviewed.

subject.description: The token subject who opened it.

BreakGlassList.description: Unreviewed grants, oldest first, up to `limit`.

more.description: True when more grants are waiting than `limit` allowed: the list is cut short and the newest are not shown.

site_time_zone.description: How the site reads times, for the review screen.

BreakGlassReview.description: Null until someone reviews the grant.

review_by.description: For a review, the next date, `YYYY-MM-DD`.

ClearReferralEntry.description: Clear a queued message. matched needs referral_id and records the link without changing the referral; dismissed names none. The reason (1 to 500 characters) is required; an entry already cleared is a 409.

ConsentRecord.description: Provisions are required for a general consent and none for a national-data-opt-out. The opt-out is held by this service only; no national check is built.

period.description: YYYY-MM-DD (UTC), both ends optional and inclusive.
YYYY-MM-DD (UTC), both ends optional and inclusive.

CreateAllergyStatement.description: State, or withdraw, "no known allergies". Refused with 422 if an active allergy exists, or if there is no statement to withdraw.

expected_version.description: The statement version last seen; 0 for none.

none_known.description: true states it; false withdraws an earlier statement.

CreateAmendment.description: A patient asks for a record to be corrected. Who asks is the token, never the body.

text.description: What should change, in the patient's words.

CreateHazard.description: Raise a hazard. Refused (422) if the title is blank or longer than 200 characters, or a rating is outside 1 to 5.

override_reason.description: Register despite likely duplicates (409 otherwise); a reason is required.

reason.description: For self or proxy, how identity was checked.

DeathAnswer.description: `not-known-to-have-died` never means the person is known to be living.

DeathOccurred.description: When the person died (`known`, with `at`), or why that is not known (`not-known`, with `reason`).

DeathReportItem.description: A report of a death that waits for a person. A pointer: no reason, source, reporter or date; a clinician or nurse reads those through the patient's route.

patient_id.description: The record to open: the surviving record, if the report was made on one merged away.

DeathReportList.description: Every report still at `reported`, oldest first, up to `limit`. The same for everyone who may read it.

accountable_role.description: The role accountable for what waits here. It names no person: the service does not know who holds it now.

more.description: True when more are waiting than `limit` allowed: the list is cut short and the newest are not shown.

DependencyReport.description: What was asked and what did not answer, as labels: database, keycloak, paseto-keys.

DuplicateConflict.description: 409 on create: likely duplicates. A candidate the caller may not see is {"restricted": true}.

Error.description: api_error.rs: RFC 9457; `detail` is fixed wording, and extra fields such as current_version or break_glass_offer may follow.

ErrorList.description: 422: the record was refused, one line per reason in `errors`.

FeedRefusal.description: One message the feed refused. `message`, the text as received, is present only when one refusal is read, never in a listing.

control_id.description: The sender's message control id (MSH-10), or ?.

event.description: The HL7 event such as A08, or ?.

reasons.description: In words; names no patient data.

more.description: True when more entries are waiting than `limit` allowed: the list is cut short and the newest are not shown.

FeedResolution.description: Null while the refusal is open.

reopened.description: How many times it was reopened.

LinkRequest.description: Merge, or unmerge, another record with the one in the path (which survives). The reason is the provenance of the change and is required. A refusal is a 422 ErrorList that may also carry `refusal` (a stable code), `refusal_into` and `conflict_codes`.

source.description: The record merged away, or to be separated again.

reason.description: Why the patient is on the list. Required.

until.description: The last day the entry holds, YYYY-MM-DD, today or later.

amendment_notices.description: By observation id; described only as an object.

ObservationRecord.description: A vital sign. A value needs a unit; no value needs an absent_reason; absence is never zero.

critical.description: Either end may be absent (unbounded); inclusive.

effective_at.description: RFC 3339; stored and returned in UTC.

range.description: Either end may be absent (unbounded); inclusive.

ObservationVersion.description: A StoredObservation plus the reason this version was written.

critical.description: Either end may be absent (unbounded); inclusive.

flag.description: Computed now; null when it cannot be said.

range.description: Either end may be absent (unbounded); inclusive.

OpenBreakGlass.description: Declare an emergency to read a record without a relationship. The reason is required; a blank one is refused (422). Asking again while a grant is open answers 200 with the same grant and does not extend it.

OverdueReviewItem.description: A need whose date to check it with the person has passed. A pointer: no code, note or reason; open the patient for those.

contact_held.description: A report of this person's death stands, confirmed or not, so nobody should contact them to check.

patient_id.description: The record to open: the surviving record, if the need was recorded on one merged away.

OverdueReviewList.description: Every active need whose date has passed, oldest date first, up to `limit`. The day is worked out in UTC.

accountable_role.description: The role that owns this list. It names no person: the rota belongs to workforce planning.

more.description: True when more are overdue than `limit` allowed: the list is cut short and the most recent dates are not shown.

OwnRecord.description: One record the caller is, or is a proxy for.

photo_version.description: Null when there is no photo or it was withdrawn.

OwnRecordList.description: Only records the full record-level decision allows; a refused one is left out (and the refusal audited).

OwnWatchList.description: The caller's own active entries, as pointers: no reason.

Patient.description: The thin identity record (the matcher's Patient). Absent evidence is null or empty, never zero.

birth_date.description: ISO 8601; may be partial (YYYY, YYYY-MM, YYYY-MM-DD).

temporary_identity.description: Set by a person for someone who cannot yet be identified. The names and birth date are then not evidence (matcher rule 7), and the record can never be linked automatically. Absent means false. Every write replaces the whole record, so a write that drops this needs a reason, or it is refused with temporary_identity_reason_required.

match_score.description: The matcher's score at merge time, if computed.

PatientView.description: A patient as read: the stored version plus the photo version, merge status and the site time zone.

photo_version.description: Null when there is no photo or it was withdrawn.

replaced_by.description: The surviving record, when this one was merged away.

PhotoVersion.description: What a photo write answers: the new version, and whether it withdrew the photo.

code.description: A code from the catalogue in `src/adjustments.rs`.

note.description: A short note. `interpreter-spoken` needs the language here.

ReferralEvent.description: The next step. The sender of the referral acts as the referrer; any other subject with the permission acts as the recipient (OQ-PC2, assumed). Refused with 422 when the state table does not allow the event, the role is wrong, or a needed note is missing.

ReferralMessage.description: An inbound referral message (an outcome, a decline, an interim note). It moves the referral it names, or is queued for a person; it is never dropped and never matched by patient and date. 200 either way.

event.description: A recipient event word such as outcome, decline or interim-note.

message.description: The message as received; required, cut at 1 MiB.

note.description: Needed by the events that need one.

referral_ref.description: The referral id as the sender wrote it. Absent or blank is queued as no-id.

ReferralMessageResult.description: moved: the referral and its new version and state. queued: the queue id and why. The message is not repeated.

ReferralQueueEntry.description: One message that did not match. `note` and `message`, as received, are present only when one entry is read, never in a listing or after a write.

reasons.description: In words; names no patient data.

more.description: True when more entries are waiting than `limit` allowed: the list is cut short and the newest are not shown.

ReferralRecord.description: The request. It does not change after it is made; the steps are in the versions.

recipient.description: The service or clinician, as the referrer names it.

replaces.description: A redirected referral of this patient that this one replaces, once (RS-2); its suspicion is carried here.

ReferralWorklistItem.description: One referral the caller sent that waits for them. A pointer: no recipient, reason, question or note; open the referral through the patient's route.

version.description: The version that waits; acknowledge this one.

why.description: reply: acknowledge it. no-response and no-outcome are timeouts (PC-3): they cannot be acknowledged and leave when the referral moves. open-suspicion: the referral has ended but its suspicion has no outcome (RS-3); it cannot be acknowledged and leaves when an outcome is recorded.

ReferralWorklistList.description: The caller's waiting referrals, oldest first, up to `limit`. `untimed` names the priorities for which no timeout is configured (OQ-PC3): a referral of that priority never goes quiet on this list.

more.description: True when more are waiting than `limit` allowed: the list is cut short and the newest are not shown.

RelationshipRecord.description: Who may treat or act for a patient. proxy is required for kind proxy and refused for every other kind.

period.description: YYYY-MM-DD (UTC), both ends optional and inclusive.

subject.description: The token sub of the person.

ResolveFeedRefusal.description: Close a refused feed message. The reason (1 to 500 characters) is required; a refusal already closed is a 409.

outcome.description: handled: the cause was fixed or the content entered another way. dismissed: it needs nothing done.

ResultRecord.description: One version of a result, as the reporting service sent it. Text fields at most 500 characters.

interpretation.description: Absent means the service said nothing, never normal.

value.description: As reported, text, so that "<0.5" survives.

version.description: The version that was signed off.

signed_version.description: When changed since sign-off: the version that was signed, to show beside the current.

ReviewBreakGlass.description: Someone else's verdict on a grant. The note is required. A grant already reviewed is a 409.

version.description: The version the signer read; an older one is a 409.

text.description: As that form version asked it.

form.description: The form version the answers were given under, and the newest version.

StoredObservation.description: The ObservationRecord fields sit beside these, not under a key.

critical.description: Either end may be absent (unbounded); inclusive.

flag.description: Computed now; null when it cannot be said.

range.description: Either end may be absent (unbounded); inclusive.

StoredReferral.description: One version of a referral. States marked provisional in spec/interoperability/closed-loop-referral.md are information-requested, deferred and redirected.

last_event.description: The event, who sent it, in which role, when, and the note.

next.description: What the state table allows next; empty in an end state.

reason.description: Why it changed; null on a first version.

carried_from.description: The redirected referral this suspicion was carried from, on version 1 of a replacement (RS-2).

reason.description: Why it was amended; null on version 1.

Suspicion.description: What the referrer suspects, under a pathway version from src/suspicion_pathways.toml. The whole suspicion is sent every time.

agreed.description: Required by a pathway that needs the person's agreement, refused by one that does not.

band.description: Required by a pathway with bands, refused by one without.

result_id.description: Required for kind result, and only then: a result on this patient's record.

point_of_suspicion.description: RFC 3339; not in the future (5 minutes' skew).

subtype.description: From the pathway version's subtype list (a primary cancer site, a type of dementia): required where the list is, refused where there is none.

outcome.description: How it ended (RS-3). Once ended, each plan's overdue is judged at the outcome, not now.

SuspicionOutcome.description: How a suspicion ends. confirmed needs diagnosis; ruled-out needs by; only confirmed carries a diagnosis or code.

detail.description: What it rests on, or why it was withdrawn.

SuspicionPlan.description: The pathway's priority and target due days for this suspicion, worked out when read. The PAS owns the reported clock.

due_on.description: YYYY-MM-DD, a day in the plan's time_zone.

time_zone.description: The site's IANA zone (EPR_SITE_TIME_ZONE): the due days are its days.

UpdateAmendment.description: One step. accept, deny, apply and extend need the clinician role; withdraw and disagree need the patient role. Each step carries its own fields: accept and extend a reason; deny a ground and a reason; apply a version; disagree a statement; withdraw none.

UpdateHazard.description: One step on a hazard, on the version last seen. `control` needs `text`; `retire` needs `evidence` and `note` and is refused with 403 unless the token holds the clinical-safety-officer role (the body never says who); `reopen` needs `reason`. Other fields for the event are refused.

expected_version.description: Any other current version is a 409.

VersionConflict.description: 409 on update: expected_version is not the current one.

state.description: lapsed: the last day has passed; worked out when read.

info.description: NOT FOR CLINICAL USE. An inventory of the served routes with their authentication and policy requirements, derived from the code. Only error bodies are described; request bodies and success responses are not. The API is versioned by the Accepts-version header; no path carries a version segment.
